figures.finding: Azerbaijan funds film through the Cinema Agency (ARKA), under the Ministry of Culture, which by its 2022 charter finances state-commissioned and state-supported national films and co-productions and picks state-funded projects by competition; its 2023-2024 competitions considered 47 projects and allocated AZN 15,112,809 to local production (AZN 167,000 of it to student films).

Overall, forty-seven film projects were presented and considered, encompassing patriotic, historical, comedic, children, and documentary content, as well as student projects. Only during 2023-2024 did the funds allocated to local film production amount to 15,112,809 manats, of which 167,000 AZN was allocated for student films. In this regard, 16 films have already been delivered; five are in the filming stage, five are in post-production, and five are in the preparation stage.

figures.finding: Azerbaijan partly reimburses a foreign producer's spend in Azerbaijan on a film: 25% where the Rules' basic conditions are met, 15% on meeting at least three of the extra cultural criteria, at most USD 1,000,000 a film in a calendar year, paid in manat at the Central Bank's official rate, from USD 200,000 spent there on a feature film (Rules approved by Cabinet Decision 196 of 4 July 2025; Decision 235 of 24 July 2026 confined them to foreign and co-produced films and changed no rate, cap or threshold). Its rate and cap weren't found in a primary until 2026-11-04.
figures.applies: AZ, foreign and co-produced films. Read by the engine from 2026-11-04: its 25%, from USD 200,000 and at most USD 1,000,000, the dollar bounds read in manat at the day's rate (money.rates), so the Azerbaijani market keeps the manat its agreements and its budget are in; until then it wasn't read, the game holding no dollar terms in a manat market. The 15% on the cultural criteria, annex 2's bonuses, the cap's calendar year (held for each film), the minimum shooting days and the share paid to Azerbaijani crew aren't read.
